## Fresh Developments (Last 24–72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM Pricing: TrendForce Q1 2026 Actuals (June 1, fresh)**
DRAM industry revenue +81% QoQ to ~$97B in Q1; conventional contract prices +93–98% QoQ — a single-quarter record. Q2 2026 forecast: +58–63% QoQ. Momentum is decelerating from the Q1 peak but remains historically elevated. HBM pre-committed tightness confirmed through 2026.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp: No new June 9 update.** SK Hynix pushed HBM4 capacity ramp from Q2 → Q3 2026 (HBM3E demand held lines longer). NVIDIA reportedly exploring relaxed HBM4 specs due to yield limits at Samsung/SK Hynix. Correction-risk thesis intact.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler Capex: No new prints.** Aggregate 2026 capex ~$725B (Alphabet/Amazon/Microsoft/Meta); no guide-down signal.

**Signal 4 — AMD/Custom ASIC: No fresh June 9 update.** MI400/Helios 2H 2026 on track. Meta unveiled 4 MTIA generations (300–500 series) through 2027. AWS Trainium3 in GA.

**Signal 5 — Optical: No fresh June 9 catalyst.** CRDO completed DustPhotonics acquisition (silicon photonics, May 2026). Lumentum received its largest-ever CPO laser purchase commitment (timing unconfirmed). InP supply gap ~70% still in play.

**Signal 6 — Solar: No fresh June 9 catalyst.** US module prices stable $0.27–0.32/W vs China $0.085–0.095/W. Section 232 tariff threat on polysilicon (~$10/kg) remains a watch item.

---

## Context vs Baseline

AVGO's miss is the first meaningful expectation reset from a top-3 custom silicon supplier this cycle — Broadcom designs custom ASICs for Google and Meta, making the signal weighted. However, CEO Hock Tan reiterated $100B+ FY2026 AI semi run-rate and flagged FY2027 momentum, pointing to timing/pace rather than demand inflection. The DRAM deceleration (Q2 +58–63% vs Q1 +93–98%) aligns with baseline correction-risk signals as all three HBM suppliers expand late-2026 capacity.

---

## Most Important Development

**AVGO −12.6% on Q3 AI chip guidance miss (SOX −5.21%)** is the headline. It is the first meaningful upside-expectation reset from a major AI silicon supplier in this cycle, pulling NVDA, MU, and MRVL sharply lower. Broadcom's held (not raised) FY $100B+ AI semi forecast suggests a demand-pace issue, not a demand-inflection — but the market is now pricing in the possibility that H2 2026 AI chip acceleration has already been largely pulled forward. Watch Q3 prints (Sep–Oct) for confirmation or reversal.
